messages:
anya: Heads-up — we need a lightweight playbook for the webinar next month and a companion battlecard that sales can use for inbound routing. Focus: how we compare vs cloud AI platforms, generic LLM APIs, and infra vendors. I sketched a draft in the doc: https://redwood.app/notes/llm-playbook :eyes:
sam: thanks, anya. can we keep the battlecard to 1 page (A4) and a short 3-bullet pitch per persona (startup eng, enterprise platform, infra buyer)?
jordan: +1 on the 3 bullets. For the benchmark narrative, recommend leading with predictable latency + cost controls (batching, cache, quantization). Cloud vendors sell scale, we sell predictable economics.
mike: for inbound routing — recommend tags: "high-latency-sensitive", "on-prem-required", "budget-conscious". If prospect selects on-prem -> route to AE with private deployment expertise.
olivia: from eng side, can provide a one-liner about our runtime: "GPU-optimized runtime with smart routing, automatic prefix caching, and quantization profiles". That should sit in the TL;DR.
anya: perfect. can someone draft the 3 bullets per persona? keep them tactical (what they care about + single proof point). I can combine into the slide.
jordan: draft bullets: 1) Startup eng: "ship fast with hosted API, predictable per-token economics, plug-and-play open models" (proof: 20% lower cost on short-churn prompts vs X in our microbench). 2) Enterprise product: "SLA-backed dedicated pools + audit logs for compliance" (proof: private customers on PD with 99.95% uptime). 3) Platform/infra buyers: "Consistent runtime across hosted/dedicated/private to reduce ops overhead" (proof: single API, no infra rewrites).
sam: love those. add a short objection handling line for each (e.g., "but cloud already has scale" -> "we abstract scale while keeping predictable economics and graceful fallbacks").
mike: for the routing rules, here's a tiny config snippet we can use in the demo lead form:

```
if lead.requirements.includes("on-prem") then route->private-AE
elif lead.api_volume > 500k then route->dedicated-sales
else route->self-serve-flow
```

useful for ops to wire into HubSpot.
bench-bot: benchmark summary: hosted-gen p50 latency 110ms (1k tokens), cost/unit 0.006/token, vs CloudY p50 140ms, cost/unit 0.0075/token — test env: gpt-style-16b, seq=1024, batching=auto.
anya: bench numbers look good. jordan — can you paste the one-sentence methodology for the battlecard footnote?
jordan: methodology: "standardized prompt suite across 3 representative workloads (chat, summarization, rerank); identical input tokens and sequence lengths; optimized kernels and quant profiles applied to all tested models."
olivia: quick ask: include a short fallback play in the battlecard: primary model -> low-latency variant -> cheap quantized fallback. Customers like to see a plan for outages/capacity spikes.
sam: webinar hooks: 1) "How we made inference costs predictable at scale" 2) "Avoiding surprise latency: routing & caching strategies" 3) panel w/ customer on dedicated migrations. Which one should be the hero?
mike: hero needs to drive demo requests. "Predictable costs" resonates with procurement. push that as hero.
anya: agreed — hero: predictable costs. sam, can you own a 45s teaser for social and a 6-slide webinar lead gen deck? mike will own routing in HubSpot.
sam: on it — I'll drop a draft teaser by EOD. linking a Figma starter: https://figma.redwood/llm-webinar-teaser
mike: I'll add the routing tags + AE assignments in HubSpot and share the mapping here by tomorrow.
anya: final ask: sales one-pager + 1-min script for SDR outreach. mike, jordan — collab?
jordan: will do the mini script. sample intro: "We help teams avoid surprise inference bills while improving tail latency — can we run a 15-min cost/latency audit for your top prompt set?"
mike: perfect. i'll prep the SDR template and add tracking params.
anya: awesome team — let's reconvene after sam posts the teaser. :thumbsup:
